title: PhaseCoder: Microphone Geometry-Agnostic Spatial Audio Understanding for Multimodal LLMs
claim: A geometry-aware spatial encoder runs in parallel to the standard mono audio encoder, and both token streams feed one LLM.
layout: Single panel, left-to-right, two parallel encoder branches feeding one LLM box
description: A single left-to-right system diagram. At left, three black microphone icons labeled 'Microphone array' sit above three grayscale waveforms. A 'mono' line from the waveforms goes to a blue triangle labeled 'Audio encoder'. Three blue token pills then lead by a solid arrow into a gray 'Multimodal LLM' box at the top right. In parallel, each channel's waveform and a separate 'mic coordinates' input feed a larger red triangle labeled 'PhaseCoder' (bold). The red triangle emits three red token pills. A dashed line carries them up into the bottom of the LLM box. A legend at bottom right labels the red pill 'tokens'. Blue and red colors separate the existing pathway from the new spatial one.
caption: Overall system diagram. The spatial audio tokens are injected into the LLM alongside the existing "mono" audio tokens.
abstract: Current multimodal LLMs process audio as a mono stream, ignoring the rich spatial information essential for embodied AI. Existing spatial audio models, conversely, are constrained to fixed microphone geometries, preventing deployment across diverse devices. We present PhaseCoder, a transformer-only spatial audio encoder that is agnostic to microphone geometry. PhaseCoder takes raw multichannel audio and microphone coordinates as inputs to perform localization and produces robust spatial embeddings. We demonstrate that Gemma 3n LLM can be fine-tuned to reason over "Spatial Audio Tokens" produced by PhaseCoder. We show our encoder achieves state-of-the-art results on microphone-invariant localization benchmarks and, for the first time, enables an LLM to perform complex spatial reasoning and targeted transcription tasks from an arbitrary microphone array.
